finding.claim: A caller-supplied _id on GridFS upload lets an attacker collide with an existing file's _id; the failed insert triggers abort(), which deletes all chunks with files_id equal to that _id, corrupting the victim file.
finding.source: _id upload option passed through Bucket::openUploadStream/uploadFromStream (src/GridFS/Bucket.php:594-611, 709-715) into WritableStream::__construct (src/GridFS/WritableStream.php:96,133) without type or ownership checks.

trace.note: uploadFromStream(filename, source, options) accepts caller options including _id
context already has collectionWrapper so resolver is skipped
_id taken from caller options without validation
insertChunkFromBuffer writes chunks with files_id = attacker _id
insertChunk fails on unique (files_id,n) index for colliding id
deleteChunksByFilesId(victim _id) removes victim chunks; no ownership check
empty upload path: close() goes straight to fileCollectionInsert
duplicate files _id on insert also triggers abort()

finding.guards_checked: Unique indexes on chunks (files_id,n) and files _id (CollectionWrapper.php:288-299, 323-337) make the insert fail but do not prevent abort(). abort() only swallows DriverRuntimeException from the delete itself (WritableStream.php:239-240), not scoped to this upload. No _id type or ownership validation anywhere on the path. Precondition: application passes client-controlled _id into upload options; not verified by running against a MongoDB server (code-reading only).
